questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.
questions.explanation: Tailgating (following too closely) causes many motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent attention than cars. Before riding on busy roads or highways, check that everything works correctly.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Take it directly onto the highway.
Practice in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all controls are. Practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is on the left side of the lane, near the center line.
Is on the right side of the lane, near the curb.
Changes based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is best all the time. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Move your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: What footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group together while giving each rider enough space. Use a single-file line when turning, curving, or entering/leaving the road.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Leather gloves provide the best grip and protection for your hands.

questions.question: You should keep a larger following distance:

options.text: If you can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance to at least four seconds if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket for motorcycle riding, look for one that is:

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Always wear protective apparel when riding. Choose a jacket that covers your arms, fits snugly, and allows movement. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If you have one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills can be affected by the first drink. Any amount of alcohol is not safe before riding.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes when you stop.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:
questions.explanation: Most collisions between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. The main cause is drivers failing to give the right-of-way to motorcyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride on the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid open doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to move if conditions change.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medicines are not very strong.
May affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding ability and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medicines, including over-the-counter and prescription drugs, have side effects that can impair your riding. Ask your doctor how any new medicine might affect your riding ability.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving over bridge gratings. You should:

options.text: Speed up to get across faster.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Zigzagging is dangerous.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing anytime you ride.

questions.question: Where is the biggest danger of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The biggest danger is at intersections. Other cars turning left in front of motorcycles cause many accidents.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcycle most visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is best. It puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Be ready to change positions if needed for safety.

questions.question: How should you brake when making a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Can motorcyclists use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes?
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, motorcyclists can use HOV lanes anytime, even with just one rider.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass. A dashed line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when flashing lights are on at a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your turn signal when you finish your turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: What should motorcyclists do about the oily strip in the center of traffic lanes?

options.text: Find the lane with the least oil buildup.

questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of lanes. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can stay to the left or right side and still be in the center portion of the lane.
